name: Medium and long term analyses
summary: Chart analyses covering roughly 1-6 months and 1-6 quarters.
details: Computer-generated chart analyses. Medium term uses an 18-month chart for a 1-6 month horizon; long term uses a 6-year chart for a 1-6 quarter horizon.
Built with pattern recognition, statistics and maths, applying traditional technical analysis with no human judgment.
Each analysis gets one of five ratings: Positive Candidate, Weak Positive, Wait/Watch, Weak Negative, Negative Candidate.
Published after the exchange closes and before the next open.

name: Short term analyses
summary: Chart analyses covering roughly 1-6 weeks.
details: Uses a 5-month chart for a 1-6 week horizon.
A separate 21-day candlestick chart, combined with the short and medium charts, suits a 0-10 day horizon.

name: Overall analysis
summary: Combines the long, medium and short term views into one assessment.
details: Combines short, medium and long term views.
Some places show a Technical score (-100 to +100) instead of, or next to, the five-step rating.

name: Buy and sell signals
summary: Concrete buy/sell signals generated for individual stocks.
details: Signals from price formations are assumed to show which way most investors are moving.
Each signal has a quality score (0-100) and an objective (target price); see Ranking by signals.

name: Trend signals
summary: Stocks that have recently entered a rising or falling trend.
details: Lists stocks that recently entered a rising or falling trend, either because the drawn trend changed or because price moved into the channel from outside.
Fields: days in trend, rising rate in degrees (0 flat to 90 vertical) and rising rate in percent (gain if the stock keeps following the channel for a year).
Simple use: buy a stock after a fresh rising-trend signal and hold until it leaves the trend.

Investtech's study (1996-2015, mainly Norway/Sweden): stocks entering rising trends averaged about 5.5% over the following months, falling-trend entries about 0.9%, versus about 3.6% for the indices. These are averages; single stocks vary.

name: Ranking by signals
summary: Overview of the latest buy and sell signals.
details: Screening list of recent positive, negative or neutral signals, filterable by indicator and by short, medium or long horizon.
Columns: date, indicator, quality (0-100 fit to an ideal pattern; below 40 is not drawn on charts) and objective (target price roughly reachable over a period as long as the pattern).
Can be used to find triggered setups or to scan for new candidates.

name: Hausse indices
summary: Indicators of how optimistic the market is.
details: A sentiment gauge from 0 to 100: the share of companies whose latest Trading Range signal is a buy (price broke above a prior top) rather than a sell (broke below a prior bottom).
Two versions: short term (hausse1, holders of 1-6 weeks) and long term (hausse2, holders of months to years).
Above 50 means most investors are positive; below 50 means optimism is low. Rising after a bottom means growing optimism.

90 or more is 'elation' (good news priced in, possible overheating; consider selling when it drops back under 90). 10 or less is 'dejection' (selling may be nearly exhausted; consider buying when it rises back over 10).
Short-term investors often react first, so the short-term index can hint at long-term turns early.

name: Candlesticks
summary: Candlestick analysis used for short-term price and volume reading.
details: Short-term price and volume tool. Each candle is one session: the body spans open to close (white if close above open, black if below) and the wicks mark the high and low.
Volume columns are green (close rose), red (close fell) or blue (unchanged).
Volume should confirm price: tall green on up days with short red on down days is positive; the reverse is negative.
Mostly white candles suggest buying in the morning and selling in the evening; mostly black candles suggest the opposite.
Formations such as the hammer give short-term buy or sell signals.

name: Pivot points
summary: Tops and bottoms in the price chart.
details: Turning points (tops and bottoms) detected by computer. A bottom is confirmed only after price moves away from it by enough: a big percentage move needs few days, a small one must hold for more days.
Used as a stock-picking list of new bottoms within your time frame, then checked with normal chart analysis.
More reliable when the move comes on rising volume and goes with the prevailing trend.
A candidate for further analysis, not a standalone buy signal.

name: Trend and trend channels
summary: Direction of price movement, e.g. a rising trend channel.
details: Trend is the prevailing price direction and, per Investtech, the most important input to the technical score.
Shown as a channel with a floor and ceiling; entering or leaving it generates trend signals.

name: Support and resistance
summary: Price levels where a stock may stall, reverse or break through.
details: Price levels where buying or selling pressure tends to halt a move; a break of such a level can start a new move.
One of the inputs to the technical score.

name: Price patterns
summary: Chart formations used to read investor direction.
details: Chart formations (for example rectangles) read as signs of which way most investors are moving.
Each carries a quality score (0-100), and the objective gives a reference target.

name: Volume
summary: Trading volume as confirmation of price moves.
details: Shares traded, used to judge how strong a price move is. Part of the technical score and used in candlestick and pivot-point confirmation.
The Volume Balance (VolBal, 22-day) compares volume with price movement.

name: Stock selection
summary: Stock-picking tool with filters such as liquidity and time perspective.
details: Screener that ranks stocks across chosen markets and sectors with sliders in three groups: General (size, liquidity, volatility), Technical (trend, support/resistance, volume, pattern signals) and Financial (P/E, P/S, P/B, yield).
Technical score runs -100 to +100: below -50 negative candidate, -50 to -25 weak negative, -25 to 25 watch, 25 to 50 weak positive, above 50 positive candidate.
Other columns: market cap, liquidity (average daily turnover), volatility (average monthly high-low range), RSI21 and VolBal.
Use technical filters for timing and financial ones for valuation, compare to the Mean and Median rows, and check liquidity before acting.

name: Trading opportunities
summary: Stocks where several indicators combine to suggest a likely rise or fall.
details: Rare setups where several indicators line up to suggest a large move with high upside and relatively low downside. Ten types, each viewable short, medium or long term.
Score 0-100 measures fit to the setup type; only 70+ are listed by default. Risk is not part of the score.
Potential is the percent upside from buy price to target; risk/reward compares upside to the stop-loss distance (for example 20% up against 5% down is about 4:1).
The detail page gives buy price, target, stop loss, time horizon and factors that strengthen or weaken the case.

name: Seasonal variations
summary: Statistical patterns in a stock's behavior across the year.
details: Shows how a stock has statistically moved across the calendar year, with a six-month projection of the average path and one and two standard-deviation bands.
Averages use a geometric mean; a monthly view shows the average change per month, and five past years show how much results vary.
A description of past patterns, not a forecast; a few extreme years can distort the average.

name: Compare stocks
summary: Compare a stock's price development with other securities.
details: Compares a stock's price development with other securities. The help page for this one was not read.

name: Health Check
summary: Detailed check of a portfolio's technical condition.
details: Portfolio health check. The linked page actually describes Top 50, so this tool's own help was not read.

name: Top 50
summary: Ranking of the 50 most positive and most negative stocks.
details: The 50 stocks with the highest technical scores, with switchable Buy and Sell candidate lists and short, medium, long or overall horizons (some need higher subscriptions).
Score inputs: trend (most important), support and resistance, price formations and volume; the weighting is not published.
Scores close together mean little; an 80 is not clearly better than a 70.

name: Today's Case
summary: A selected technically positive stock.
details: A selected technically positive stock. No help page was found.

summary: Daily automated evaluations.
details: Daily automated evaluations. No help page was found.

details: Notifications when a stock reaches a set price. No help page was found.
